{"parentUuid":"f51d1681-7de6-4fa2-a435-ac683e92680e","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- empirical-probe-first: Probe ALL viable strategies in a multi-option ladder BEFORE committing to one. Use when a session-plan / decision-ADR / spec presents ≥3 strategy options (e.g. \"Strategy A1/A2/A3\" or \"alternative B/C/D\") and the recommended option's source-evidence may be stale. Outputs a probe matrix per strategy + commit decision with empirical citation. Pairs with `vendor-api-probe.sh` (deterministic detection layer; SessionStart hook) and `decompose-work` (deterministic-vs-LLM split per probe). Charter promotion target — codifies L-S32-1 doctrine surfaced at S32 Track A pivot (master-plan recommended A2 vnstock alternate; empirical probe rejected A1+A2; A3 SSI direct httpx adopted instead).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- hook-diagnostics: Inspect hook event lifecycle (state machine + transcript cache + aggregator output) when triaging failed/stuck hooks or auditing self-awareness rollups. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- session-memory-l0-l1: Extract structured memories (L0 quick metadata + L1 deep) from a Claude Code session JSONL transcript. L0 is pure regex (file paths, commands, errors, failures incl. Vietnamese phrases, next step). L1 ships the prompt builder + response parser + 15+35 head/tail windowing — caller dispatches the LLM (no auto-invoke in Phase 0). Plus cleanText harness-stripper + TranscriptCache (mtime+size dual-check + LRU). Use when ingesting a session for memory promotion, computing what files/commands/failures the session touched, or preparing an offline LLM extraction.\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n- sync-pull: On-demand confidence-score lookup before a SCOPE+/ARCH/IMPL decision. Output drives \"self-decide vs grill\" choice. Use whenever an agent is about to commit a non-trivial decision and needs to ground confidence in historical hit rate per Charter Principle 8 (Calibration over confidence).\n- test-pyramid-balance: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\n- try-n-approaches: Karpathy autoresearch outer-loop framing — given a task or signal, generate ≥3 distinct approaches (DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON families), pick one per cheap-first ordering, attach a deterministic metric function (per L-S12-1), and write the experiment frame to learning-data/loop/. Everything here represents **agent state, decisions, plans, observations, learning**. Agents WRITE here freely (within constitution rules); humans READ here but normally do not edit.\n\nThis separation exists to prevent two failure modes from orch:\n1. **Charter drift via shared-workspace mutation** (orch CF-DOGFOOD-2)\n2. **Human cognitive overload from dense session logs** (UP02 §1.3 — \"human đối mặt hàng chục spec/document quá tải nếu không sắp xếp khoa học\")\n\nThe agent owns this directory but must keep it AUDITABLE — every artifact provenance-linked, every decision sourced.\n\n---\n\n## Subdirectories\n\n| Path | Purpose | Lifecycle |\n|---|---|---|\n| `constitution/` | **IMMUTABLE without explicit user approval**. Charter-tier rules (autonomous-protocol, model-routing, identity-scope, etc.). Track 7 produces drafts in `proposals/`; user explicit approve to move here. | Edit denied by .claude/settings.json; Write only via human approval gate |\n| `memory/project.md` | High-level project state; phase tracker; ADRs (last 5). Update on phase boundaries + architectural decisions. | Long-lived; trim to most recent decisions |\n| `memory/current-execution.md` | **THE single routing source of truth**. Active phase + active session + autonomous_mode flag + routing table. Read FIRST every session. | Long-lived; updated each session boundary |\n| `memory/agent-notes.md` | Learned rules from real experience (post-mortem / drift / user correction). Append-only mostly. | Long-lived |\n| `memory/decisions/` | Sequential ADRs (`NNN-<slug>.md`) + `_template.md` + `README.md` index. 12-field schema (Track 2). | Append-only; supersession via status field |\n| `memory/sessions/` | One file per session: `YYYY-MM-DD-session-N.md`. What happened, decisions made, files touched. | Append-only |\n| `memory/observations/` | Subagent return artifacts (per Track 6 spec). Each subagent writes one observation file describing what it did. | Append; cleaned periodically by aggregator |\n| `memory/checkpoints/` | Session handoff state for self-reboot (Track 5). `latest.md` is canonical pointer; timestamped historical files retained. | Append + latest.md updated each checkpoint |\n| `memory/patterns-discovered/` | Pattern mining outputs (Track 0 — DONE) + ongoing pattern catalog. | Append; significant patterns promoted to constitution |\n| `memory/drift-logs/` | Drift-check (DR1-DR12) results; runs on hook + on-demand. | Time-series append |\n| `memory/post-mortems/` | After significant failure or thesis-revoked event: what failed, root cause, prevention rule. | Append |\n| `memory/thesis-log/` | Stock-domain thesis exploration entries. Read-only for IMPL sessions. | Append + revisited per calibration |\n| `memory/sync-tracker/` | Track 8a output: Confidence Score SQLite + weights.yaml + auto-rendered `_index.md`. | Live updated by hooks |\n| `memory/self-awareness/` | Track 9 output: model × effort × thinking profile cards + known-issues + best-practices. | Live updated by Stop-hook aggregator |\n| `memory/mistake-log.md` | Track 7 deliverable: structured failure catalog. What went wrong / Root cause / Prevention rule / Severity. | Append; pre-flight read by all agents |\n| `session-plans/pending/` | Plans authored, awaiting execution. Phase 0 plan lives here. | Move to `completed/` when done |\n| `session-plans/completed/` | Executed plans; archived for reference + retrospective input. | Append |\n| `quality-reports/{deterministic,probabilistic,drift-reports}/` | Tier-1/2/3 gate outputs (CLAUDE.md § Quality Gates). | Per-run files |\n| `ubiquitous-language/` | DDD glossary + domain-mapping + drift-log. Stockforge stock-domain vocabulary. | Append; canonical via `/drill-me` |\n| `calibration/` | Empirical hit-rate data per signal type. Confidence claims MUST trace here (CLAUDE.md hard rule). | Append per thesis post-mortem |\n| `research/` | Research notes from `research-scanner` subagent dispatches (e.g., reference-repo studies). | Append |\n\n---\n\n## Contract Rules (BINDING)\n\n1. **Constitution is immutable absent explicit human approval.** `Edit/Write` to `agent-workspace/constitution/**` is in `.claude/settings.json` deny list. Track 7 writes constitution drafts to `proposals/`; user explicit approve moves them.\n\n2. **`memory/decisions/` is append-mostly + supersession-status.** Don't delete decisions; mark `status: superseded-by-D-NNN` to revoke. Sequential numbering (`001`, `002`, ...) — don't reuse numbers.\n\n3. **`current-execution.md` is the routing source-of-truth.** No skill, agent, or command may hardcode phase paths or session paths from memory; resolve via this file. Stale paths in CLAUDE.md or skills = anti-pattern.\n\n4. **Never edit `obsidian-vault/raw/`.** Immutable. Vault writes only to `wiki/`. (Established in stockforge CLAUDE.md.)\n\n5. **Provenance is mandatory.** Every decision file references its source (human prompt / spec clause / drift detection / agent inference). Every thesis cites source + as-of date (I-S2). (Otherwise they're informal notes, not contracts.)\n\n---\n\n## Reading Priority for Agent\n\nPer `agent-workspace/constitution/autonomous-protocol.md` (Track 7) and stockforge `CLAUDE.md` § Session Protocol:\n\n1. **`memory/current-execution.md`** — first; resolve active track\n2. **`memory/project.md`** — project state\n3. **`memory/checkpoints/latest.md`** if a recent checkpoint exists (within last 24h) — resume context\n4. **`memory/agent-notes.md`** — learned rules\n5. **`memory/mistake-log.md`** — pre-flight failure catalog\n6. **Last 3 files in `memory/sessions/`** — recent context\n7. **`session-plans/pending/<active-plan>.md`** — current plan\n8. **Relevant constitution files** as task demands (don't load all every session)\n9. **Relevant skills + agents + commands** as task demands\n\n---\n\n## Anti-Patterns to Avoid\n\n(From `memory/patterns-discovered/SYNTHESIS.md` § 6, full catalog 23 items. Highest-priority for this directory:)\n\n- **AP-1 Same-agent self-review** — never review your own implementation; dispatch fresh-context verifier\n- **AP-2 Self-track wind-down** — `.transcript-tokens` real-transcript is authoritative, not LLM self-track\n- **AP-5 Charter-coherence defer overriding user-CRITICAL** — re-read all `user_prompt/*` at every phase entry; never silently defer USER-CRITICAL\n- **AP-7 Performative SC ticking** — defer with explicit prerequisites > fire vacuous proposals\n- **AP-8 Pre-staged work causing checkpoint drift** — update `current-execution.md` immediately on task complete, not session-end\n- **AP-17 Identity drift** — stockforge is AI-first VN stock advisory; not generic financial framework (see `constitution/identity-scope.md` once Track 7 ships)\n- **AP-23 Continuous LLM-Guardian** — deterministic hooks = Guardian; LLM Guardian only at session-end aggregation\n\n---\n\n## Connection to human-workspace/\n\nThis directory is the agent's domain. Human's domain is `human-workspace/`. The two communicate through:\n- Human → Agent: `human-workspace/user_prompt/`, `human-workspace/decisions/`\n- Agent → Human: `human-workspace/notifications/`, `human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/`\n- Bidirectional: `human-workspace/q-and-a/answered/` — agent writes pending; either human or agent (per Auto-mv rule below) moves resolved bundles to answered/\n- Audit trail: this directory's `memory/decisions/` references `human-workspace/` source files via path pointers\n\n**Auto-mv rule (HH-E.2 — D-031 ratification, 2026-05-05)**: Agent MAY mv a bundle from `q-and-a/pending/` to `q-and-a/answered/` IFF ALL of the following hold:\n\n1. **Frontmatter signal**: bundle frontmatter `status:` field value starts with one of: `answered-`, `closed-`, `resolved-`. Examples already in repo: `answered-via-chat`, `answered-via-AskUserQuestion`, `answered-2026-05-04-via-chat`. Detection is deterministic (head -20 of file + grep `^status:`).\n2. **No human-veto signal**: bundle frontmatter has NO `wait_until:` ISO-8601 timestamp greater than current epoch — if present, agent MUST defer mv until that timestamp passes. Allows human to override auto-mv per-bundle without contract amendment.\n3. **No global pause**: file `human-workspace/q-and-a/.auto-mv-paused` does NOT exist — global kill switch for the auto-mv mechanism (single empty file presence pauses all auto-mv).\n4. **Hook validation**: the mv is performed by `scripts/hooks/qa-pending-auto-mover.sh` (Stop hook). The decision's `status` field becomes e.g. `ACCEPTED-REV-2`, and a new section `## Amendments` accumulates change history.\n\nWhen a decision is **wholly** replaced, do NOT amend — author a new decision file `D-NNN` with `supersedes: D-MMM`, and set the original's `status: SUPERSEDED-BY-D-NNN` and `superseded_by: D-NNN`.\n\nRule of thumb:\n- ≤30% content change, scope/intent unchanged → amend in-place (REV-N)\n- > 30% content change, or scope/intent changed → new decision file with supersedes pointer\n\n---\n\n## Naming Convention\n\n`<NNN>-<kebab-case-slug>.md` where `NNN` is zero-padded 3-digit (`001`, `002`, ... `999`).\n\nSlug rules:\n- ≤ 60 chars\n- Lower-case ASCII + hyphens only\n- Verb-leading when describing a change (`pause-orch`, `split-track-8`); noun-leading when describing a system (`provenance-protocol`, `confidence-score-system`)\n\n---\n\n## Provenance Discipline (binding)\n\nEvery decision MUST cite its `source_evidence`. An empty `source_evidence: []` triggers a drift-detector flag (`DR-PROV` — to be wired in Track 5 hooks).\n\nAcceptable source types:\n1. `human-workspace/user_prompt/<file>.txt` — user's explicit direction\n2. `human-workspace/decisions/<file>.md` — user's strategic decision\n3. `human-workspace/q-and-a/answered/<file>.md` — user's reply to Q&A bundle\n4. `agent-workspace/memory/patterns-discovered/*.md` — pattern mining result\n5. `agent-workspace/memory/post-mortems/<file>.md` — failure-driven learning\n6. `agent-workspace/memory/drift-logs/<file>.md` — drift signal evidence\n7. `specs/**/*.md` — formal spec clause\n8. Decisions are never deleted; they are marked `SUPERSEDED-BY-D-NNN` or `REVOKED` and remain on disk as the audit trail.\n\n---\n\n## Status Legend\n\n| Status | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `PROPOSED` | Authored by agent; awaiting user confirmation. Open Q&A bundle may exist. |\n| `ACCEPTED` | User confirmed (via chat phrase, `user_prompt/` file, or `q-and-a/answered/` reply). Decision is binding. |\n| `SUPERSEDED-BY-D-NNN` | A later decision replaced this one. Pointer in `superseded_by` field. The replacement decision's `supersedes` field points back. |\n| `REVOKED` | Reversed without replacement. Triggers post-mortem (`agent-workspace/memory/post-mortems/`). 6-step protocol from Q&A A6 applies. |\n\nA decision may also carry `REV-N` amendments (in-place edits) — see [Amendments Convention](#amendments-convention) below.\n\n---\n\n## Decision Levels (per Q&A A4 thresholds)\n\n| Level | Confidence threshold to self-decide without Q&A | Examples |\n|---|---|---|\n| `CHARTER` | 0.99 | Identity scope, mission rewrite, autonomous mode activation |\n| `SCOPE` | 0.90 | Phase plan, multi-track design, BC count, port-list scope |\n| `ARCH` | 0.80 | Library choice, schema design, hook architecture |\n| `IMPL` | 0.50 | File layout inside a track, naming, refactor pass |\n\nIf agent confidence is below threshold for a level, it MUST open a Q&A bundle in `human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/` rather than self-decide.\n\n---\n\n## Sequential Index\n\n> Newest first. The decision's `status` field becomes e.g. `ACCEPTED-REV-2`, and a new section `## Amendments` accumulates change history.\n\nWhen a decision is **wholly** replaced, do NOT amend — author a new decision file `D-NNN` with `supersedes: D-MMM`, and set the original's `status: SUPERSEDED-BY-D-NNN` and `superseded_by: D-NNN`.\n\nRule of thumb:\n- ≤30% content change, scope/intent unchanged → amend in-place (REV-N)\n- > 30% content change, or scope/intent changed → new decision file with supersedes pointer\n\n---\n\n## Naming Convention\n\n`<NNN>-<kebab-case-slug>.md` where `NNN` is zero-padded 3-digit (`001`, `002`, ... `999`).\n\nSlug rules:\n- ≤ 60 chars\n- Lower-case ASCII + hyphens only\n- Verb-leading when describing a change (`pause-orch`, `split-track-8`); noun-leading when describing a system (`provenance-protocol`, `confidence-score-system`)\n\n---\n\n## Provenance Discipline (binding)\n\nEvery decision MUST cite its `source_evidence`. An empty `source_evidence: []` triggers a drift-detector flag (`DR-PROV` — to be wired in Track 5 hooks).\n\nAcceptable source types:\n1. `human-workspace/user_prompt/<file>.txt` — user's explicit direction\n2. `human-workspace/decisions/<file>.md` — user's strategic decision\n3. `human-workspace/q-and-a/answered/<file>.md` — user's reply to Q&A bundle\n4. `agent-workspace/memory/patterns-discovered/*.md` — pattern mining result\n5. `agent-workspace/memory/post-mortems/<file>.md` — failure-driven learning\n6. `agent-workspace/memory/drift-logs/<file>.md` — drift signal evidence\n7. `specs/**/*.md` — formal spec clause\n8. Charter section reference (`PROJECT_CHARTER.md § X.Y`)\n\nDecisions that derive from agent inference alone (no upstream evidence) MUST tag `level: IMPL` AND state inference chain in `chosen_rationale`.\n\n---\n\n## R7 Mitigation: Defer-Cycle Tracking\n\nPer Decision 002 REV-2 § C R7 (msmdp Decision Provenance Chain pattern):\n\n- Each time a decision is paused, postponed, or rolled forward, increment `defer_cycles` by 1.\n- `defer_cycles > 3` → drift-detector raises alert; human Q&A bundle required to either commit or revoke.\n- `re_attempt_prereq` documents what must change before the decision can be resumed (e.g. \"blocker on D-XYZ resolution\", \"user feedback on Q-S5\", \"telemetry data after 1 month\").\n\nThis prevents the **can-kicking** anti-pattern observed during ms-mdp-admin Phase 2 workflow review.\n\n---\n\n## Reading Order for New Agents\n\n1. Decisions are never deleted; they are marked `SUPERSEDED-BY-D-NNN` or `REVOKED` and remain on disk as the audit trail.\n\n---\n\n## Status Legend\n\n| Status | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `PROPOSED` | Authored by agent; awaiting user confirmation. Open Q&A bundle may exist. |\n| `ACCEPTED` | User confirmed (via chat phrase, `user_prompt/` file, or `q-and-a/answered/` reply). Decision is binding. |\n| `SUPERSEDED-BY-D-NNN` | A later decision replaced this one. Pointer in `superseded_by` field. The replacement decision's `supersedes` field points back. |\n| `REVOKED` | Reversed without replacement. Triggers post-mortem (`agent-workspace/memory/post-mortems/`). 6-step protocol from Q&A A6 applies. |\n\nA decision may also carry `REV-N` amendments (in-place edits) — see [Amendments Convention](#amendments-convention) below.\n\n---\n\n## Decision Levels (per Q&A A4 thresholds)\n\n| Level | Confidence threshold to self-decide without Q&A | Examples |\n|---|---|---|\n| `CHARTER` | 0.99 | Identity scope, mission rewrite, autonomous mode activation |\n| `SCOPE` | 0.90 | Phase plan, multi-track design, BC count, port-list scope |\n| `ARCH` | 0.80 | Library choice, schema design, hook architecture |\n| `IMPL` | 0.50 | File layout inside a track, naming, refactor pass |\n\nIf agent confidence is below threshold for a level, it MUST open a Q&A bundle in `human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/` rather than self-decide.\n\n---\n\n## Sequential Index\n\n> Newest first. The decision's `status` field becomes e.g. `ACCEPTED-REV-2`, and a new section `## Amendments` accumulates change history.\n\nWhen a decision is **wholly** replaced, do NOT amend — author a new decision file `D-NNN` with `supersedes: D-MMM`, and set the original's `status: SUPERSEDED-BY-D-NNN` and `superseded_by: D-NNN`.\n\nRule of thumb:\n- ≤30% content change, scope/intent unchanged → amend in-place (REV-N)\n- > 30% content change, or scope/intent changed → new decision file with supersedes pointer\n\n---\n\n## Naming Convention\n\n`<NNN>-<kebab-case-slug>.md` where `NNN` is zero-padded 3-digit (`001`, `002`, ... `999`).\n\nSlug rules:\n- ≤ 60 chars\n- Lower-case ASCII + hyphens only\n- Verb-leading when describing a change (`pause-orch`, `split-track-8`); noun-leading when describing a system (`provenance-protocol`, `confidence-score-system`)\n\n---\n\n## Provenance Discipline (binding)\n\nEvery decision MUST cite its `source_evidence`. An empty `source_evidence: []` triggers a drift-detector flag (`DR-PROV` — to be wired in Track 5 hooks).\n\nAcceptable source types:\n1. `human-workspace/user_prompt/<file>.txt` — user's explicit direction\n2. `human-workspace/decisions/<file>.md` — user's strategic decision\n3. `human-workspace/q-and-a/answered/<file>.md` — user's reply to Q&A bundle\n4. `agent-workspace/memory/patterns-discovered/*.md` — pattern mining result\n5. `agent-workspace/memory/post-mortems/<file>.md` — failure-driven learning\n6. `agent-workspace/memory/drift-logs/<file>.md` — drift signal evidence\n7. `specs/**/*.md` — formal spec clause\n8. Charter section reference (`PROJECT_CHARTER.md § X.Y`)\n\nDecisions that derive from agent inference alone (no upstream evidence) MUST tag `level: IMPL` AND state inference chain in `chosen_rationale`.\n\n---\n\n## R7 Mitigation: Defer-Cycle Tracking\n\nPer Decision 002 REV-2 § C R7 (msmdp Decision Provenance Chain pattern):\n\n- Each time a decision is paused, postponed, or rolled forward, increment `defer_cycles` by 1.\n- `defer_cycles > 3` → drift-detector raises alert; human Q&A bundle required to either commit or revoke.\n- `re_attempt_prereq` documents what must change before the decision can be resumed (e.g. \"blocker on D-XYZ resolution\", \"user feedback on Q-S5\", \"telemetry data after 1 month\").\n\nThis prevents the **can-kicking** anti-pattern observed during ms-mdp-admin Phase 2 workflow review.\n\n---\n\n## Reading Order for New Agents\n\n1. S246 sandwich-dev executes it. No code is written here.\n19\t\n20\t---\n21\t\n22\t## 1. Root-cause restatement (empirical)\n23\t\n24\t### 1.1 What the post-S244 hook actually wrote at runtime\n25\t\n26\t`agent-workspace/memory/.claude-instance.lock` (live file, captured at 21:32+07:00 by S245 — see observation `2026-05-10-S245-lock-pid-secondary-defect.md` lines 17-18):\n27\t\n28\t```\n29\tsession=unknown:1:1778421770\n30\t```\n31\t\n32\tFormat per `scripts/hooks/single-claude-instance-lock.sh:31`:\n33\t```bash\n34\techo \"session=${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID:-unknown}:${SELF_PID}:$(date +%s)\" > \"$LOCK\"\n35\t```\n36\t\n37\tThus empirically:\n38\t- `CLAUDE_SESSION_ID` env var → empty → fallback `unknown` fired.\n39\t- `SELF_PID = ${CLAUDE_PID:-$PPID}` (line 20) → resolved to `1`. Therefore both `CLAUDE_PID` was empty AND `$PPID` of the bash hook script was `1`.\n40\t\n41\t### 1.2 Why this defeats BLOCK detection\n42\t\n43\t`scripts/hooks/single-claude-instance-lock.sh:22-28`:\n44\t```bash\n45\tif [ -f \"$LOCK\" ]; then\n46\t  HOLDER_PID=\"$(awk -F: '{print $2}' \"$LOCK\" 2>/dev/null)\"\n47\t  if [ -n \"$HOLDER_PID\" ] && tasklist //FI \"PID eq $HOLDER_PID\" 2>/dev/null | grep -qi \"claude.exe\"; then\n48\t    echo \"[BLOCK] ...\"\n49\t    export STOCKFORGE_AUTONOMOUS_DISABLE=1\n50\t    exit 2\n51\t  fi\n52\tfi\n53\t```\n54\t\n55\tWith `HOLDER_PID=1`:\n56\t- `tasklist //FI \"PID eq 1\"` returns Windows kernel processes (System Idle Process / System), never `claude.exe`.\n57\t- `grep -qi \"claude.exe\"` → false → BLOCK does NOT fire.\n58\t- Subsequent claude.exe overwrites lock at line 31, proceeds. Phantom-dispatch protection bypassed.\n59\t\n60\t### 1.3 Provenance for \"CLAUDE_SESSION_ID empty on Windows\"\n61\t\n62\tThis is NOT a guess — it is established with explicit evidence in three places:\n63\t\n64\t- `scripts/hooks/profile-template-auto-populate.sh:38` (comment): \"$CLAUDE_SESSION_ID env (which is empty in **174/174 SessionStart events** on Windows Claude Code 4.x; auto-populate residue investigation finding).\"\n65\t- `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md:547` — L-S48m-1 ACTIVE: \"Per-session-marker hooks NOT use $CLAUDE_SESSION_ID env on Windows\" (HIGH severity).\n66\t- `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md:591` — L-S108-1 ACTIVE: \"${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID:-WORD} → empty on Windows → fallback 'WORD' shared across all sessions → permanent idempotency lockout.\"\n67\t- `scripts/hooks/dispatch-jsonl-recorder.sh:104-110` — explicitly documents this and uses **stdin JSON `SESSION_ID`** instead. This is the canonical workaround pattern in this repo.\n68\t- Live evidence: `agent-workspace/memory/.session-hooks.log:26` shows `Stop session=` (empty value) — direct empirical reproduction.\n69\t\n70\t### 1.4 What is NOT yet established\n71\t\n72\t- WHY `$PPID == 1` inside the bash hook subprocess — three plausible RC paths (S245 observation lines 47-50):\n73\t  - (a) Claude Code TUI on Windows spawns hook bash with `setsid` / `nohup` style detach.\n74\t  - (b) Claude Code uses a Windows job-object pattern that orphans the bash subprocess.\n75\t  - (c) The intermediary launcher (e.g. git-bash → bash.exe wrapper) re-parents to PID 1 (init / systemd-equivalent / git-bash session leader).\n76\t  - **Without knowing which**, any \"use `$PPID`\" or \"walk parent chain\" mitigation is speculative.\n77\t\n78\tThis uncertainty is why **Section 2 (Investigation) MUST run before Section 5 (Implementation).**\n79\t\n80\t---\n81\t\n82\t## 2. Root-cause restatement (empirical)\n\n### 1.1 What the post-S244 hook actually wrote at runtime\n\n`agent-workspace/memory/.claude-instance.lock` (live file, captured at 21:32+07:00 by S245 — see observation `2026-05-10-S245-lock-pid-secondary-defect.md` lines 17-18):\n\n```\nsession=unknown:1:1778421770\n```\n\nFormat per `scripts/hooks/single-claude-instance-lock.sh:31`:\n```bash\necho \"session=${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID:-unknown}:${SELF_PID}:$(date +%s)\" > \"$LOCK\"\n```\n\nThus empirically:\n- `CLAUDE_SESSION_ID` env var → empty → fallback `unknown` fired.\n- `SELF_PID = ${CLAUDE_PID:-$PPID}` (line 20) → resolved to `1`. Therefore both `CLAUDE_PID` was empty AND `$PPID` of the bash hook script was `1`.\n\n### 1.2 Why this defeats BLOCK detection\n\n`scripts/hooks/single-claude-instance-lock.sh:22-28`:\n```bash\nif [ -f \"$LOCK\" ]; then\n  HOLDER_PID=\"$(awk -F: '{print $2}' \"$LOCK\" 2>/dev/null)\"\n  if [ -n \"$HOLDER_PID\" ] && tasklist //FI \"PID eq $HOLDER_PID\" 2>/dev/null | grep -qi \"claude.exe\"; then\n    echo \"[BLOCK] ...\"\n    export STOCKFORGE_AUTONOMOUS_DISABLE=1\n    exit 2\n  fi\nfi\n```\n\nWith `HOLDER_PID=1`:\n- `tasklist //FI \"PID eq 1\"` returns Windows kernel processes (System Idle Process / System), never `claude.exe`.\n- `grep -qi \"claude.exe\"` → false → BLOCK does NOT fire.\n- Subsequent claude.exe overwrites lock at line 31, proceeds. Phantom-dispatch protection bypassed.\n\n### 1.3 Provenance for \"CLAUDE_SESSION_ID empty on Windows\"\n\nThis is NOT a guess — it is established with explicit evidence in three places:\n\n- `scripts/hooks/profile-template-auto-populate.sh:38` (comment): \"$CLAUDE_SESSION_ID env (which is empty in **174/174 SessionStart events** on Windows Claude Code 4.x; auto-populate residue investigation finding).\"\n- `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md:547` — L-S48m-1 ACTIVE: \"Per-session-marker hooks NOT use $CLAUDE_SESSION_ID env on Windows\" (HIGH severity).\n- `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md:591` — L-S108-1 ACTIVE: \"${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID:-WORD} → empty on Windows → fallback 'WORD' shared across all sessions → permanent idempotency lockout.\"\n- `scripts/hooks/dispatch-jsonl-recorder.sh:104-110` — explicitly documents this and uses **stdin JSON `SESSION_ID`** instead. This is the canonical workaround pattern in this repo.\n- Live evidence: `agent-workspace/memory/.session-hooks.log:26` shows `Stop session=` (empty value) — direct empirical reproduction.\n\n### 1.4 What is NOT yet established\n\n- WHY `$PPID == 1` inside the bash hook subprocess — three plausible RC paths (S245 observation lines 47-50):\n  - (a) Claude Code TUI on Windows spawns hook bash with `setsid` / `nohup` style detach.\n  - (b) Claude Code uses a Windows job-object pattern that orphans the bash subprocess.\n  - (c) The intermediary launcher (e.g. git-bash → bash.exe wrapper) re-parents to PID 1 (init / systemd-equivalent / git-bash session leader).\n  - **Without knowing which**, any \"use `$PPID`\" or \"walk parent chain\" mitigation is speculative.\n\nThis uncertainty is why **Section 2 (Investigation) MUST run before Section 5 (Implementation).**\n\n---\n\n## 2. Investigation step (BEFORE fix) — probe script\n\n### 2.1 Goal\n\nEmpirically determine, on real Claude Code on Windows, what process-tree state the hook subprocess actually has access to. Output is a written artifact that captures:\n\n| Signal | Source | Why it matters |\n|---|---|---|\n| `$$` | bash hook | The hook's own PID |\n| `$PPID` | bash hook | What S245 saw as `1` — confirm |\n| `ps -ef` snapshot | git-bash builtin | Walk upward to find a `claude.exe` ancestor (if any) |\n| `tasklist //V` (no filter) | Windows | Authoritative live `claude.exe` PID(s) and command line(s) |\n| `wmic process where \"name='claude.exe'\" get ProcessId,ParentProcessId,CommandLine` | Windows fallback | Parent-of-claude.exe (may be `cmd.exe` or VS Code terminal) |\n| All env vars matching `CLAUDE_*` / `STOCKFORGE_*` / `SESSION*` | bash hook | Discover any populated identity var the TUI does export |\n| stdin JSON payload (full) | bash hook | `dispatch-jsonl-recorder.sh:109` already proves `SESSION_ID` is reliably in stdin JSON; want to confirm `pid`/`ppid`/`hook_event_name` fields too |\n\n### 2.2 Probe deliverable (NOT a fix — diagnostic only)\n\n**File**: `scripts/hooks/lock-rc-probe.sh` (NEW, temporary diagnostic).\n\n**Behavior**: Runs identically to `single-claude-instance-lock.sh` but writes a richer diagnostic file to `agent-workspace/memory/observations/lock-rc-probe-<timestamp>.txt` containing all signals from §2.1 above. Each will fire SessionStart. Two diagnostic files appear (one per window). Compare.\n\n### 2.3 Decision rule from probe output\n\n| Probe finding | Implication for fix |\n|---|---|\n| `ps -ef` reveals a `claude.exe` ancestor (any depth) | Mitigation (c) — walk ps -ef upward — is viable + cheap |\n| stdin JSON contains a usable `pid` / `parent_pid` / `process` field | Best signal; use stdin (cheapest, most reliable, no Windows-shell dep) |\n| Neither — only `tasklist` shows claude.exe but no parent linkage from hook context | Fall back to mitigation (a): record ALL claude.exe PIDs in lock; BLOCK if any of them is alive other than self |\n| `$PPID` actually != 1 in fresh-window case but == 1 in subagent-spawn case | Confirms RC = subagent_transport `subprocess.run([\"claude\",\"-p\",...])` detach; spawn-context probe path needed |\n\n### 2.4 Probe budget\n\n~30 LOC bash + 1 settings.json edit (additive line). Without head -1, both lines reach $((..))\n  # → multi-line LAST_PROMOTE_SESSION → \"syntax error in expression\" + SESSION_DELTA unbound (S245 RC fix).\n  LAST_PROMOTE_SESSION=$(basename \"$LAST_PROMOTE_FILE\" | grep -oE 'S[0-9]+' | head -1 | tr -d 'S' || echo 0)","originalFile":"#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# promotion-cycle-trigger.sh — S35 D4 META-fix (per L-S35-1 / BP-S35-1 / decision-discipline Rule 4a draft).\n# Fires `promote-rule` subagent dispatch reminder when:\n#   (a) ≥5 sessions passed since last `agent-workspace/memory/observations/promote-rule-S*.md`, OR\n#   (b) Phase boundary detected (current-execution.md `Phase` field changed since last run).\n# Hard-block at 8 sessions / phase-cross without promotion observation.\n#\n# Wire as Stop hook in .claude/settings.json once L-S11-1 portability check (Phase 0 = bash+POSIX) passes.\n# Output goes to stderr + drift-log; non-zero exit only at hard-block.\nset -euo pipefail\ntrap 'exit 0' ERR\n\nPROJECT_DIR=\"${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}\"\nEXEC_FILE=\"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md\"\nOBS_DIR=\"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/memory/observations\"\nLOG=\"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/memory/.promotion-cycle.log\"\nmkdir -p \"$(dirname \"$LOG\")\"\n\n[ ! -f \"$EXEC_FILE\" ] && exit 0\n\n# Latest session number — scoped to ## SXX section headers (per L-S51-1 fix at S51).\n# Prior bug (M-S51-1): grepped for `**Session N**:` literal which never appears in current-execution.md\n# (file uses `## S50 — ...` header format). LATEST_SESSION was always 0; SESSION_DELTA was always\n# negative; hard-block + soft-warn rules never escalated despite 20+ fires/day.\n# Real format: `## S<NN>[a-z]? — <title>` headers (e.g. `## S50 — Phase 3.5 master-plan authored`,\n# `## S49b — Tier 1 archive sweep`). Also handle subordinate variants (S49a, S49b, S50-pre).\nLATEST_SESSION=$(grep -oE '^## S[0-9]+' \"$EXEC_FILE\" | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | sort -n | tail -1 || echo 0)\n[ -z \"$LATEST_SESSION\" ] && LATEST_SESSION=0\n\n# Latest phase number.\nLATEST_PHASE=$(grep -oE '\\*\\*Phase\\*\\*: [0-9]+' \"$EXEC_FILE\" | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || echo 0)\n\n# Find latest promote-rule observation file.\nLAST_PROMOTE_FILE=$(ls -t \"$OBS_DIR\"/promote-rule-S*.md 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)\nLAST_PROMOTE_SESSION=0\nLAST_PROMOTE_PHASE=0\nif [ -n \"$LAST_PROMOTE_FILE\" ]; then\n  # NOTE on L-S53-2 lint advice (S56 categorization, KI-S55-1 family):\n  #   bash-hook-lint Check 8 flags `grep -oE 'S[0-9]+'` here as unanchored\n  #   positional-marker → suggests `^` anchor. WRONG advice for THIS line: target\n  #   is `basename \"$LAST_PROMOTE_FILE\"` which yields strings like \"promote-rule-S52.md\"\n  #   where `S<N>` appears mid-string after the \"promote-rule-\" prefix. Anchoring\n  #   `^S[0-9]+` would NEVER match (filename starts with `p`). Categorization:\n  #   content-search of filename token (NOT header-parse). Per L-S55-1 retrofit\n  #   recipe: ratify false-positive via this comment. Lint flag persists in surface\n  #   log (acceptable per soft-warn surface).\n  LAST_PROMOTE_SESSION=$(basename \"$LAST_PROMOTE_FILE\" | grep -oE 'S[0-9]+' | tr -d 'S' || echo 0)\n  LAST_PROMOTE_PHASE=$(grep -oE 'phase: [0-9]+' \"$LAST_PROMOTE_FILE\" 2>/dev/null | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || echo 0)\nfi\n\nSESSION_DELTA=$((LATEST_SESSION - LAST_PROMOTE_SESSION))\nPHASE_CHANGED=0\n[ \"$LATEST_PHASE\" -gt \"$LAST_PROMOTE_PHASE\" ] && PHASE_CHANGED=1\n\nprintf '[%s] promotion-cycle-trigger: latest_session=%s last_promote=S%s delta=%s latest_phase=%s last_phase=%s phase_changed=%s\\n' \\\n  \"$(date -Iseconds)\" \"$LATEST_SESSION\" \"$LAST_PROMOTE_SESSION\" \"$SESSION_DELTA\" \"$LATEST_PHASE\" \"$LAST_PROMOTE_PHASE\" \"$PHASE_CHANGED\" >> \"$LOG\"\n\n# Hard-block: ≥8 sessions OR phase-changed without promote.\nif [ \"$SESSION_DELTA\" -ge 8 ] || { [ \"$PHASE_CHANGED\" -eq 1 ] && [ \"$SESSION_DELTA\" -ge 1 ]; }; then\n  printf '[%s] HARD-BLOCK promotion-cycle: delta=%s phase_changed=%s\\n' \\\n    \"$(date -Iseconds)\" \"$SESSION_DELTA\" \"$PHASE_CHANGED\" >> \"$LOG\"\n  echo \"promotion-cycle HARD-BLOCK: ≥8 sessions OR phase boundary crossed without promote-rule run. Dispatch promote-rule subagent before next session-end.\" >&2\n  exit 0  # non-blocking; advisory only — hard-block via Stop-hook decision JSON in v2\nfi\n\n# Soft-warn: ≥5 sessions.\nif [ \"$SESSION_DELTA\" -ge 5 ]; then\n  printf '[%s] SOFT-WARN promotion-cycle: delta=%s — recommend running promote-rule subagent\\n' \\\n    \"$(date -Iseconds)\" \"$SESSION_DELTA\" >> \"$LOG\"\n  echo \"promotion-cycle SOFT-WARN: ${SESSION_DELTA} sessions since last promote-rule run; recommend dispatching subagent.\" >&2\nfi\n\nexit 0\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":44,"oldLines":7,"newStart":44,"newLines":10,"lines":["   #   content-search of filename token (NOT header-parse). AP-23 4-instance threshold MET (overdue from instance #2).\n26\t**Rule**: When `autonomous_mode=true` and >1 claude.exe runs concurrently in the same project, each instance independently consumes routing inputs and dispatches its own copy of work. **Process-level mutual exclusion via `single-claude-instance-lock.sh` SessionStart hook is now BINDING.** Hook holds a session-lifetime lock at `agent-workspace/memory/.claude-instance.lock`; SessionEnd hook cleans it. No `trap` on EXIT in the hook script (S244 fix: that defeats the lock).\n27\t**Anti-example** (M-S238-2 / S243): two parents both running autonomous-mode → both dispatch sandwich-verifier → composite observation file with redundant content. Lock with line-30 EXIT trap removed lock immediately after creation, defeating the design.\n28\t**Correct example**: post-S244 hook holds lock until SessionEnd hook removes it; 2nd parent's SessionStart sees live lock + emits `[BLOCK]` + exit 2 + sets `STOCKFORGE_AUTONOMOUS_DISABLE=1`.\n29\t**Why**: Cross-session phantom claudes from `continue-injector.ps1` SendKeys + `budget-watchdog.sh` cliff-auto-reboot via `session-self-reboot.sh`. {"parentUuid":"988167a7-ffca-44b8-b6d0-78b4020d188f","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_01P7pkw7MRaxXMSHBGP1rofb","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01LcwR88csPHb8nDEt2vph4i","name":"Edit","input":{"replace_all":false,"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\agent-workspace\\memory\\agent-notes.md","old_string":"### 2026-05-10 (S245): Phantom-dispatch cross-session race — L-S240-5 PROMOTED to HOOK","new_string":"### 2026-05-10 (S245): Two new AP-23-family harness defects — env-prefix-fails-spawn + grep-multi-S-token — L-S245+-2/3\n**Context**: Both surfaced from user-displayed TUI errors mid-S245 turn. (1) `.claude/settings.json` lines 204/208/212/277/281/285 used `CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT=X bash \"...\"` env-prefix syntax — Claude Code's hook spawn layer fails this with `bash: CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT=...: No such file or directory` (3 SessionStart + 3 UserPromptSubmit hooks all silently broken since add; harness-health log last entry 20:43:40 confirms zero production fires post-add). process.stdin.on('data',c=>s+=c);\nprocess.stdin.on('end',()=>{\n  try { const p=JSON.parse(s); console.log(p.session_id||''); }\n  catch { console.log(''); }\n});\" 2>/dev/null || true)\"\n  [ -n \"$_sid\" ] && SESSION_ID=\"$_sid\"\nfi\n\n# ── Collect current claude.exe PIDs via tasklist ──────────────────────────────\n# Uses //NH (no header) //FO CSV (CSV output) for reliable column parsing.\n# Filters IMAGENAME eq claude.exe (per single-claude-instance-lock.sh original line 24 bare-tasklist usage).\n# //V (verbose) adds command-line column so we can exclude subagent spawns (claude -p / --print).\n# Precedent: plan §6.2 confirms bare 'tasklist' (not absolute path) is correct.\n_tasklist_out=\"$(tasklist //NH //FO CSV //V //FI \"IMAGENAME eq claude.exe\" 2>/dev/null || true)\"\n\n# Parse PID column (field 2 in CSV) and filter out subagent spawns.\n# CSV row: \"claude.exe\",\"PID\",\"Session Name\",\"Session#\",\"Mem Usage\",\"Status\",\"User Name\",\"CPU Time\",\"Window Title\"\n# CommandLine is NOT a separate column in tasklist //V CSV — Window Title is the last column.\n# We filter by checking if the raw row contains ' -p ' or ' --print ' pattern (subagent dispatch argv).\n# Precedent: plan §4.3 counter-argument 4 + plan §3.6 mechanism spec.\nCURRENT_PIDS=\"\"\nwhile IFS= read -r line; do\n  [ -z \"$line\" ] && continue\n  # Extract PID: field 2 after stripping CSV quotes.\n  _pid=\"$(printf '%s' \"$line\" | awk -F'\",\"' '{gsub(/^\"|\"$/,\"\",$2); print $2}' 2>/dev/null || true)\"\n  [ -z \"$_pid\" ] && continue\n  # Exclude subagent spawns: look for -p or --print in window title / any field (best-effort).\n  # tasklist //V CSV window title is the last quoted field — subagent spawns show \"N/A\" or blank.\n  # The actual filtering that matters: the subagent claude.exe is a separate PID; Check liveness.\n      # Count stored pids.\n      STORED_COUNT=0\n      for _p in $(printf '%s' \"$STORED_PIDS_CSV\" | tr ',' ' '); do\n        STORED_COUNT=$(( STORED_COUNT + 1 ))\n      done\n\n      # Count current pids.\n      CURRENT_COUNT=0\n      for _p in $(printf '%s' \"$CURRENT_PIDS\" | tr ',' ' '); do\n        CURRENT_COUNT=$(( CURRENT_COUNT + 1 ))\n      done\n\n      # Check if any stored PID is still alive in current tasklist.\n      LIVE_SIBLING=0\n      for _stored_pid in $(printf '%s' \"$STORED_PIDS_CSV\" | tr ',' ' '); do\n        [ -z \"$_stored_pid\" ] && continue\n        for _cur_pid in $(printf '%s' \"$CURRENT_PIDS\" | tr ',' ' '); do\n          if [ \"$_stored_pid\" = \"$_cur_pid\" ]; then\n            LIVE_SIBLING=1\n            break\n          fi\n        done\n        [ \"$LIVE_SIBLING\" -eq 1 ] && break\n      done\n\n      if [ \"$LIVE_SIBLING\" -eq 1 ]; then\n        # Self-identification heuristic (plan §3.1):\n        # If current count > stored count: a NEW claude.exe joined → that new one is us → BLOCK.\n        # If current count == stored count: same set of processes (we ARE the stored session) → no BLOCK.\n        # If current count < stored count: some stored pids died → they are not all alive → liveness\n        #   check above would have missed (but we already set LIVE_SIBLING=1, so re-evaluate).\n        if [ \"$CURRENT_COUNT\" -le \"$STORED_COUNT\" ];
